question.question:
Apply only this fictional scenario-local retirement plan. A saver starts with zero savings and makes end-of-year deposits for 7 years. The first deposit, at the end of year 1, is 14500 USD; each later deposit is 4 percent larger than the previous year's deposit. The balance earns 3.5 percent per year, credited at each year end before that year's deposit is added. At the end of year 5, immediately after that year's deposit, the saver withdraws 6500 USD once; the remaining balance keeps compounding. The retirement target is 120000 USD in today's purchasing power and is inflated at 2 percent per year compounded over all 7 years. Shortfall is the larger of the inflated target minus the projected end-of-year-7 balance and zero. To close any shortfall, the saver would add a level extra deposit at the end of each year from the year after the withdrawal year through year 7 inclusive, earning the same 3.5 percent return. The top-up factor is the sum of the end-of-year-7 compounded values of one USD deposited at each of those year ends. The required extra annual deposit equals shortfall divided by the top-up factor and is zero when there is no shortfall. Report the projected balance, inflated target, shortfall and top-up factor.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `usd_per_year` with no unit label or additional text.

Report nonnegative shortfall of projected balance versus inflated target.
Report compounded value sum of one USD deposited each top-up year end.
